done_looks_like: Running `config-diff a.json b.json` on examples/{a,b}.json prints a numbered, JSON-path-keyed diff to stdout; the diff matches examples/expected-diff.txt byte-for-byte.

The CLI accepts user-entered numeric indices (comma- or space-separated) selecting which diff entries to apply; invalid input is rejected with a clear error referencing the bad token and exit code != 0.
After accepted selection, the tool writes a.patched.json byte-identical to examples/expected-patched.json; original a.json and b.json are unmodified (read-only against inputs).
Malformed or unreadable input files produce a single-line stderr message naming the offending file plus the underlying parse/IO reason, and the process exits non-zero without writing any output file.

Exit code is 0 on successful patch write, non-zero on parse/IO/selection error; stdout diff is grep-able (one diff entry per line, prefixed with stable index + path) so the tool composes into shell pipelines.

MODULE src/config_diff/diff_model.py (applicability: dto — opt-out of C1-C8 per foundation.md §3 row 'Pure data container'). Role: DiffEntry / PatchPlan dataclasses carrying {path, kind, left_value, right_value} and the ordered list of selected entries; no behavior beyond construction.

MODULE src/config_diff/differ.py (applicability: business-logic). hides_decision: 'how a tree-shaped JSON value pair is linearised into an ordered, JSON-path-keyed sequence of added/removed/changed entries with stable ordering across runs'. Entry-point budget: 1 (`compute_diff(left: dict, right: dict) -> list[DiffEntry]`). Strategy seam: none (single algorithm; YAGNI per Pocock two-adapter rule). Broad interface: invariants=both inputs must be JSON-parsed dict|list|scalar (not raw bytes); ordering=entries are sorted by JSON path lexicographically so output is deterministic across runs; error_modes=raises DifferError(path, reason) only — no stdlib exception propagates. Bounded context: config-diff (this is the canonical BC for diff vocabulary).

MODULE src/config_diff/applier.py (applicability: business-logic). hides_decision: 'how a selected subset of DiffEntry items is folded back into the left tree to produce a new tree, without mutating the input and preserving key order of unchanged subtrees'. Entry-point budget: 1 (`apply_patch(left: dict, plan: PatchPlan) -> dict`). Strategy seam: none. Broad interface: invariants=left argument is never mutated (returned tree is a deep copy with selected edits applied); ordering=resulting key order matches left for unchanged keys, follows right for newly added keys; error_modes=raises ApplierError(path, reason) when a selected DiffEntry path no longer resolves in left. Bounded context: config-diff. Deletion test: removing this module would force the path-walk + immutable-update logic to regrow inside cli.py and inside any future programmatic caller (e.g. an apply-without-prompt mode) — two distinct callers, C3 passes.

MODULE src/config_diff/cli.py (applicability: framework-shaped — opt-out of C1-C8 per foundation.md §3 row 'Framework-mandated shape (CLI command)'). Role: typer entrypoint wiring stdlib json.load → differ.compute_diff → numbered-print → prompt-for-indices → applier.apply_patch → json.dump, plus stderr/exit-code shaping. No business logic beyond glue.
